newsitem.title: UK: LCE cocoa slips below support as longs sell.
newsitem.headline: LCE cocoa slips below support as longs sell.

text.p: London cocoa futures broke out of their recent range and stood stubbornly below key support on Friday as disappointed longs sold, traders said.
Traders said the slide of the second-month December contract past the 1,020 mark to 1,015 stg could be part of a corrective move and the 1,020-1,040 range could be reinstated next week.
"Today could just be a freak day," said one trader.
A weak close on Thursday had discouraged the longs and speculators after failure to chase up from an earlier high of 1,056 stg basis December, they said.
But sentiment was also dampened by talk that one crop forecaster pegged the Ivorian main harvest at 900,000 tonnes in 1996/97, slightly higher than earlier assessments.
December closed at 1,019 stg a tonne, down 13 stg on the day while front-month September shed 19 stg to 995 stg a tonne but ended above a low of 993 stg.
Turnover on the Exchange totalled 5,207 lots, mainly in outright volume. Switches included Sept/Dec at 20 stg and Dec/March at 11 stg, traders said.

Technical analysts said the prospects for the mild rally to extend did not look good after the third-month March faced was rejected by earlier highs. "The sideways trend could stay in place for some time yet," said Elli Gifford of Investment Research in a weekly summary.
The London market will be closed for a bank holiday on Monday and re-open on Tuesday, August 27.
